- name: marketo__change_data_scd
      description: Type 2 SCD of lead attributes with daily versions, backfilling email/first/last via field-level flags, row-only values for company/lead_status, and a deterministic surrogate key.
      grain: Rows per lead_id per valid_to date from the unioned snapshot and change data; no enforced uniqueness.
      source_models:
      - intermediate.marketo__change_data_pivot
      - intermediate.int_marketo__lead
      - intermediate.marketo__change_data_details
      business_logic: '- Read sources: - leads: current lead snapshot (one row per lead as of today). - change_data: historical daily changes by lead and date. - details: field-level boolean flags by lead and date indicating whether a field change boundary exists. - Build the unioned set: - From leads: emit one row per lead with date_day = today; populate email/first_name/last_name; set other fields (e.g., company, lead_status) to null. - Union all rows from change_data (one per lead_id and date_day) with their recorded values. - Prepare partitions for backfill: - valid_to equals the row’s date_day (today for snapshot rows; change date for change_data rows). - Join details on lead_id and date_day. - For each of email, first_name, and last_name, compute a descending-date group number per lead that increases on every row except when both conditions hold: the field value is null and the corresponding details flag is false. These groups define contiguous runs across which missing values should be carried backward. - Backfill fields: - For email, first_name, and last_name: within each lead and group, carry the most recent non-null value (from the later date in that group) backward to earlier dates; if a group has no non-null value, the field remains null. - Non-backfilled fields: - company and lead_status take only the value present on that specific row/date; values are not carried across dates and nulls remain null. - Surrogate key: - lead_day_id is the MD5 hash of lead_id and valid_to concatenated with an underscore; nulls are treated as empty strings. - Output columns: valid_to, lead_id, email_c, first_name_c, last_name_c, company_c, lead_status_c, lead_day_id. No de-duplication is applied; multiple rows may exist for a lead and date if both sources supply that date.'
      columns:
      - name: valid_to
        data_type: DATE
        description: Version date equal to the row’s date_day (today for snapshot rows; the change date for historical rows).
      - name: lead_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Lead identifier carried through from the unioned inputs.
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: email_c
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Email after carrying the latest available value backward within groups that continue only when the field is null and the details flag is false; otherwise the group breaks; remains null if no later non-null exists.
      - name: first_name_c
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: First name after carrying the latest available value backward within groups that continue only when the field is null and the details flag is false; otherwise the group breaks; remains null if no later non-null exists.
      - name: last_name_c
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Last name after carrying the latest available value backward within groups that continue only when the field is null and the details flag is false; otherwise the group breaks; remains null if no later non-null exists.
      - name: company_c
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Company value taken only from the same row/date; no cross-date fill; nulls preserved.
      - name: lead_status_c
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Lead status taken only from the same row/date; no cross-date fill; nulls preserved.
      - name: lead_day_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Deterministic MD5 hash of lead_id and valid_to joined by '_' with nulls treated as empty strings.
        tests:
        - not_null

      description: Daily lead field history built from a calendar spine joined to change data at valid_to, with values carried backward from change days.

      - intermediate.marketo__change_data_scd
      - intermediate.marketo__lead_calendar_spine

      columns:

        data_type: DATE

        tests:
        - not_null

set to 0 if sends are 0. - email_click_rate_pct: clicks divided by sends, multiplied by 100, rounded to two decimals; set to 0 if sends are 0. - total_lead_score: opens*5 plus clicks*10. - Derive segmentation per lead_id from the aggregated metrics: - rfm_segment by total_lead_score: Champion (>=100), Loyal Customer (>=50), Potential Loyalist (>=25), Regular Subscriber (>=10), At Risk (>=5), else Inactive. - value_tier by total_lead_score: Platinum (>=80), Gold (>=50), Silver (>=25), Bronze (>=10), else Basic. - lead_quality_tier by rates: A-Tier (open>=50 and click>=10), B-Tier (open>=30 and click>=5), C-Tier (open>=15), D-Tier (open>=5), else Unqualified. - Join lead_base to email_engagement and lead_segmentation with left joins on lead_id. - Default handling: - Counts, distincts, rates, and score are set to 0 if no engagement data is found. - rfm_segment defaults to "Unknown", value_tier to "Basic", and lead_quality_tier to "Unqualified" when segmentation is missing. - first/last timestamps remain null if the event never occurred. - days_since_last_* are the calendar days between the date of the last event and today; set to 9999 if the last event is missing. - lead_tenure_days is the calendar days between the lead''s created date and today. - lead_health_status (in order): Healthy if score>=50 and last open within 30 days; Good if score>=25 and within 60 days; Fair if score>=10 and within 90 days; Poor if score>=5; else Critical. - next_best_action (in order): Schedule Sales Call if click rate>=10 and last click within 7 days; Send Product Demo if open rate>=30; Re-engagement Campaign if last open is over 60 days ago and there has been at least one open; Welcome Series if there have been no opens; else Standard Campaign Flow. - last_updated_at is set to the current timestamp at query execution with time zone.'

- name: marketo__leads
      description: Lead dimension combining base Marketo profile with merge/delete flags and aggregated email engagement metrics.
      grain: One row per lead_id
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_marketo__lead
      - staging.stg_marketo__activity_merge_leads
      - staging.stg_marketo__activity_delete_lead
      - marts.marketo__email_sends
      business_logic: '- Start from staging.stg_marketo__lead (one row per lead_id). - From staging.stg_marketo__activity_merge_leads, for each lead_id, combine merged_lead_ids into a single string separated by ", " after removing duplicates; missing values are ignored and ordering is not enforced. - Identify deleted leads as the set of lead_ids appearing in staging.stg_marketo__activity_delete_lead. - Enrich the base leads via left joins: - is_deleted is true when the lead_id appears in the deleted set; otherwise false. - merged_into_lead_id is the combined string of merged IDs for the lead; null when none exist. - is_merged is true when merged_into_lead_id is populated; otherwise false. - Compute email engagement metrics from marts.marketo__email_sends grouped by lead_id: - count_sends equals the total number of send records for the lead. - count_opens, count_bounces, count_clicks, count_deliveries, count_unsubscribes are the sums of their respective per-send counters; missing values in those counters do not contribute. - count_unique_opens equals the number of unique email_send_id values with an open event. - count_unique_clicks equals the number of unique email_send_id values with a click event. - Records without email_send_id do not contribute to the unique counts. - Left join the email metrics to the enriched leads by lead_id and set all email metrics to 0 when no send records exist or the aggregate is missing. - Emit all base lead fields plus the flags and email metrics; exactly one row per lead_id.'
      columns:
      - name: lead_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Unique lead identifier from stg_marketo__lead; one row per lead_id.
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: created_timestamp
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Creation timestamp from stg_marketo__lead, passed through as a string.
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: updated_timestamp
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Last update timestamp from stg_marketo__lead, passed through as a string.
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: email
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Email address from stg_marketo__lead, passed through as-is.
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: first_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: First name from stg_marketo__lead; may be NULL.
      - name: last_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Last name from stg_marketo__lead; may be NULL.
      - name: is_deleted
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: True if the lead_id appears in stg_marketo__activity_delete_lead; otherwise false.
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: merged_into_lead_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Comma-separated merged_lead_ids per lead after removing duplicates; missing values ignored; NULL when none; ordering unspecified.
      - name: is_merged
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: True when merged_into_lead_id is populated; otherwise false.
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: count_sends
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Total email send records for the lead; 0 when none.
        tests:
        - not_null
        - count_sends >= 0
      - name: count_opens
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Sum of per-send opens for the lead; missing values ignored; 0 when none.
        tests:
        - not_null
        - count_opens >= 0
      - name: count_bounces
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Sum of per-send bounces for the lead; missing values ignored; 0 when none.
        tests:
        - not_null
        - count_bounces >= 0
      - name: count_clicks
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Sum of per-send clicks for the lead; missing values ignored; 0 when none.
        tests:
        - not_null
        - count_clicks >= 0
      - name: count_deliveries
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Sum of per-send deliveries for the lead; missing values ignored; 0 when none.
        tests:
        - not_null
        - count_deliveries >= 0
      - name: count_unsubscribes
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Sum of per-send unsubscribes for the lead; missing values ignored; 0 when none.
        tests:
        - not_null
        - count_unsubscribes >= 0
      - name: count_unique_opens
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of unique email_send_id values with an open event; records without identifiers ignored; 0 when none.
        tests:
        - not_null
        - count_unique_opens >= 0
      - name: count_unique_clicks
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of unique email_send_id values with a click event; records without identifiers ignored; 0 when none.
        tests:
        - not_null
        - count_unique_clicks >= 0

cte_definitions.sql: SELECT CAST(COUNT(*) AS BIGINT) AS total_campaigns, CAST(COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE open_rate >= 25) AS BIGINT) AS healthy_campaigns, CAST(COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE open_rate < 5) AS BIGINT) AS critical_campaigns, CAST(COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE bounce_rate > 10) AS BIGINT) AS campaigns_with_bounce_issues FROM (SELECT campaign_id, AVG(CASE WHEN was_opened THEN 100.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS open_rate, AVG(CASE WHEN was_bounced THEN 100.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS bounce_rate FROM marts.marketo__email_sends WHERE NOT campaign_id IS NULL GROUP BY campaign_id) AS c

cte_definitions.name: lead_rows
cte_definitions.sql: SELECT l.lead_id, es.activity_id, es.was_clicked, es.was_opened, es.was_delivered, es.count_opens, es.count_clicks FROM intermediate.int_marketo__lead AS l LEFT JOIN marts.marketo__email_sends AS es USING (lead_id) WHERE NOT l.is_deleted AND NOT l.is_merged

cte_definitions.name: lead_summary
cte_definitions.sql: SELECT CAST(COUNT(*) AS BIGINT) AS total_leads, CAST(COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE NOT activity_id IS NULL AND was_clicked) AS BIGINT) AS engaged_leads, CAST(COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE NOT activity_id IS NULL AND was_opened AND NOT was_clicked) AS BIGINT) AS moderately_engaged_leads, CAST(COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE NOT activity_id IS NULL AND NOT was_opened) AS BIGINT) AS low_engaged_leads, CAST(COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE activity_id IS NULL) AS BIGINT) AS inactive_leads, ROUND(CAST(COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE NOT activity_id IS NULL AND was_clicked) AS DOUBLE) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) * 100, 2) AS engaged_leads_pct, ROUND(CAST(COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE activity_id IS NULL OR NOT was_delivered) AS DOUBLE) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) * 100, 2) AS at_risk_leads_pct, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN activity_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE COALESCE(count_opens, 0) * 5 + COALESCE(count_clicks, 0) * 10 END), 2) AS avg_lead_score FROM lead_rows

cte_definitions.name: combined
cte_definitions.sql: SELECT CURRENT_DATE AS health_check_date, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP AS health_check_timestamp, d.*, COALESCE(x.total_email_attempts, 0) AS total_email_attempts, COALESCE(x.successful_deliveries, 0) AS successful_deliveries, COALESCE(x.total_bounces, 0) AS total_bounces, COALESCE(x.overall_delivery_rate_pct, 0) AS overall_delivery_rate_pct, COALESCE(x.overall_bounce_rate_pct, 0) AS overall_bounce_rate_pct, COALESCE(x.recent_delivery_rate_pct, 0) AS recent_delivery_rate_pct, l.*, c.*, ROUND(CASE WHEN c.total_campaigns = 0 THEN 0 ELSE CAST(c.healthy_campaigns AS DOUBLE) / c.total_campaigns * 100 END, 2) AS healthy_campaigns_pct FROM daily_summary AS d CROSS JOIN deliverability AS x CROSS JOIN campaign_summary AS c CROSS JOIN lead_summary AS l

      source_models:
      - marts.marketo__email_sends

if total = 0 then 0. - daily_open_rate_pct = opened / delivered * 100; if delivered = 0 then 0. - daily_bounce_rate_pct = bounced / total * 100; if total = 0 then 0. - Compute system_health_indicators over daily_email_volume: - system_volume_classification from the average daily_emails_sent: ≥1000 High Volume System; ≥500 Medium Volume System; ≥100 Low Volume System; else Minimal Volume System. - delivery_rate_volatility, open_rate_volatility, bounce_rate_volatility are the standard deviations of the corresponding daily percentage metrics. - delivery_stability from the standard deviation of daily_delivery_rate_pct: ≤5 Stable; ≤10 Moderate Variance; else High Variance. - days_of_data = number of daily rows; earliest_activity_date = minimum activity_date; latest_activity_date = maximum activity_date. - Compute deliverability_health across all marts.marketo__email_sends: - Totals: total_email_attempts (all sends), successful_deliveries (delivery true), total_bounces (bounce true). - overall_delivery_rate_pct = delivered / attempts * 100 (2 decimals); overall_bounce_rate_pct = bounces / attempts * 100 (2 decimals). - recent_delivery_rate_pct over the last 30 days: deliveries in last 30 days / total activity in last 30 days * 100 (2 decimals); if no activity in last 30 days then 0. - Compute campaign_health by first aggregating per non-null campaign_id in marts.marketo__email_sends: - Per-campaign averages: open rate = average of opened (as percent); bounce rate = average of bounced (as percent). - Summaries: total_campaigns = distinct campaign_ids; healthy_campaigns = distinct campaigns with open rate ≥25%; critical_campaigns = distinct campaigns with open rate <5%; campaigns_with_bounce_issues = distinct campaigns with bounce rate >10%. - Compute lead_database_health from intermediate.int_marketo__lead l left joined to marts.marketo__email_sends es on lead_id, filtering out deleted or merged leads: - Counts are over the joined rows (not distinct leads): engaged_leads = rows with a match and a click; moderately_engaged_leads = rows with a match and opened but not clicked; low_engaged_leads = rows with a match and not opened; inactive_leads = rows with no matching send; total_leads = total joined rows. - engaged_leads_pct = engaged_leads divided by total joined rows * 100 (2 decimals). - at_risk_leads_pct = rows with no match or with delivery false divided by total joined rows * 100 (2 decimals). - avg_lead_score = average of (count_opens*5 + count_clicks*10) for matched rows, using 0 for no-activity leads; rounded to 2 decimals in the final output. - Final output produces a single-row snapshot with: - health_check_date and health_check_timestamp taken at query time. - deliverability_health_status from overall_delivery_rate_pct: ≥95 Excellent; ≥90 Good; ≥85 Fair; ≥80 Poor; else Critical. - lead_database_health_status from engaged_leads_pct and at_risk_leads_pct: ≥40% engaged and ≤20% at-risk = Excellent; ≥25% and ≤30% = Good; ≥15% and ≤40% = Fair; ≥5% = Poor; else Critical. - healthy_campaigns_pct = healthy_campaigns / total_campaigns * 100 (2 decimals); if total_campaigns = 0 then 0. - Recent 7-day trends as averages of daily_email_volume where activity_date is within the last 7 days; returns NULL if no such days exist. - Volatility metrics are rounded to 2 decimals. - overall_health_score is the sum of four point components based on thresholds (deliverability, engagement, campaign mix, stability); the sum is rounded and stored as an integer (range ~35–100). - primary_recommendation chosen in order: if overall_delivery_rate_pct < 85 then focus on deliverability; else if at_risk_leads_pct > 30 then re-engage leads; else if critical_campaigns > 3 then optimize campaigns; else if delivery_stability is High Variance then stabilize sending; otherwise continue current efforts.'

      - name: open_rate_volatility

      - name: bounce_rate_volatility
